Beat me... kill me, I don't care. One day or another the truth will come out... the thief of many days, one day...
notes: The proverb is left deliberately incomplete because the source stops after `ஒரு நாள்...`.

translation.english_text: Malini... you will not go......
I cannot... come and see the queen's inner chamber! What business does Satyaseelar have there at midnight?...
Ayyo! Ayyo?...
Ah!...... Is that so... truly?... (He runs. Vasanthi and the attendant laugh.)
notes: The source-attached exit and conspirators' laughter remain inside the linked turn.

source_locator.description: Padmavathi's room.

translation.english_text: Padmavathi's room.
Minister! Ask the Maharaja himself what he says!
The Maharaja will not pay attention to any of this—
When I think of Manoharan, I am afraid.
There is no need to fear—I will take care of it.

source_locator.description: The king and Vasantha Sena listen from hiding.

translation.english_text: [The king and Vasantha Sena listen from hiding.]
The Maharaja will not notice... there is no need to fear Manoharan.
notes: Vasantha Sena repeats the overheard phrases to sharpen the king's suspicion.

source_locator.description: The king turns away suspicious of Padmavathi.

translation.english_text: [The king turns away, now suspicious of Padmavathi.]

source_locator.description: A private place.

translation.english_text: [In a private place.]
(Looking at the moon) Stain... stain! A stain never before in my lineage! Sinner!
notes: The moon-gazing cue and repeated `stain` image remain inside the source-linked turn.

source_locator.description: The king smashes Padmavathi's nearby statue.

translation.english_text: [He smashes Padmavathi's statue beside him.]
Prabhu! Be calm...
Calm! Only in her death will I have calm!
notes: The repeated `அமைதி` word is preserved.

translation.english_text: Listen to this, Maharaja! The queen......
Queen...... do not say that again! Woman without honour! Vagabond... whore! Vasanthi! You yourself give the order! She must be put in the underground prison.
notes: The king's escalating insults are translated directly rather than euphemized.

translation.english_text: Putting the queen in prison will cool your fury. At the spring festival Manoharan leapt at me because I spoke ill of his mother! What will he say now? Will he ask my pardon?...
I shall make him ask... I shall make him apologize in the royal hall itself for speaking against you. Prison for Padmavathi! Manoharan must apologize to Vasantha Sena......

source_locator.description: Padmavathi's room.

translation.english_text: Padmavathi's room.
Mother must go to prison... Manoharan must apologize!
And that too in the royal hall, before that owl from the rubbish heap!
notes: `குப்பை மேட்டுக் கோட்டான்` is kept close to its concrete comic insult rather than replaced by a generic slur.

translation.english_text: The one giving the order is Father!
Yes, my dear! Do not forget that—the father who begot you.
Father... he gained a fearless-hearted son... he gained a wife of rare virtue... there is one thing he forgot to gain, Mother! Sense! Sense! That alone he forgot to gain!
notes: The repeated `அறிவு! அறிவு!` is retained for Rajapriyan's punchline.

translation.english_text: I shall remind him of what he forgot...
I am telling you that you cannot, my treasure! Appa may have erred in haste... whatever it is, go and ask the reason!
Ask the reason?
Athai... no... do not send him... no, Athai... do not send him... no, Athai... that is it—you must not go...
notes: The repeated pleading is preserved rather than compressed.

translation.english_text: Brave son... go and return...
No, Athai!
Vijaya!

I shall go and return. [To the soldiers who have come to arrest Padmavathi] Beware! Until I return, you must not go near my mother...
[To Vijaya]
Vijaya! Take care of her... I am going.
notes: Both source-attached address cues remain inside the immutable linked record.

source_locator.description: The king's court hall.

translation.english_text: The king's court hall.
A storm is about to blow, O king! This palace is going to become a mound of dust!
notes: The storm/dust warning is retained at its full theatrical pitch.

translation.english_text: Rajapriya!
Hearing the king's urgent order, Manoharan is coming like a charging battle-bull!
notes: `அடலேறு` is kept as a heroic battle-bull image rather than weakened to merely 'angry'.

translation.english_text: Ah!

He is coming calmly. But a volcano gives no warning before it roars. Prison for the queen. Manoharan must apologize! O king, can one show poison to a tiger? If a warrior is enraged, disaster will follow! Withdraw the order! Otherwise a spark will leap! A spark will leap!
notes: Volcano/tiger/spark escalation and the repeated final warning are preserved.

source_locator.description: Vasanthi trembles.

translation.english_text: (Vasanthi trembles.)
Do not be afraid! I shall see that spark! Hmm—bind him in iron chains and bring him here.
(To Manoharan) The king's order... we must bind you with this chain and bring you to the assembly.
Shackles?
Shackles! This is disaster. (To the attendant) Bring my upper cloth!

source_locator.description: Padmavathi runs out.

translation.english_text: (She runs out.)
Manohara! You are going to the assembly to ask the reason. What does it matter how you go? Shackles are for the hands, not for the mouth! (Manoharan is dragged in wearing the shackles.)
notes: The hands/mouth contrast and source-attached dragging cue remain inside the linked turn.

translation.english_text: Manohara! Do you know why I have called you?
Please correct yourself. You did not have me brought. You had me dragged here.
You will know my command.

A command—is this a command? An appetite with no shore in sight! Decking me in gold and gems and glittering diamonds, fondling me with ‘my eye! my pearl! my Tamil melody!’—on an ivory bed... in a sandalwood cradle! ‘Warrior! You who fill my eyes! You who came in the warrior line!’—the one whom you praised and cherished so... to bind that Manoharan in chains, stand him in the middle of the assembly and celebrate your joy—is the name for that unappeased desire of yours ‘a command,’ Father?
notes: The childhood endearments, ivory/sandalwood imagery and final command/desire reversal are retained without compression.

translation.english_text: Tch... tch...
You stand before justice as an accused man; at this moment you are not a son before his father!

Accused! Hmm—what harm have I done, and to whom? Who has suffered because of me? O king! I ask not as a son before his father, but as one among the subjects. Did I murder? Did I rob?... Did I do the work of a little fox overturning the country? What crime did I commit, O sovereign—what crime did I commit? Will you not say? You need not say.
Here are scholars and ministers. Here are great warriors born of the warrior clan! Representatives of the people! The pillars of this country are here. Let them say... what crime did I commit?
notes: The crime-question refrain and the scholars/ministers/warriors/representatives/pillars accumulation are retained.

translation.english_text: The Maharaja must state the crime.
This has nothing to do with you.
If it has nothing to do with the assembly, why bring it before the assembly? History meets for the first time today the strange spectacle of a family quarrel coming into the royal hall, Maharaja!
Enough, stop... for the wrong you committed at the spring festival, you must apologize to Vasantha Sena.
That is precisely why I ask the reason!
Do you know the punishment in the royal assembly for those who speak against it?
It can only be less than the punishment given to those who imprison the lawfully wedded queen and crown the one who lay in a corner.
Do not provoke my anger! Carry out the king's order—
What is a king's order? People have begun asking the reason even for God's order. O king! One who lies subdued even after hearing ‘Mother must go to prison’ is a tortoise!
notes: The God/order challenge and tortoise image are retained.

translation.english_text: Fool who knows no distinction between mother and father! Have you heard of Parasurama, who obeyed his father's command and cut off his mother's head?
Parasurama—an avatar. Manoharan—a human being!
notes: The source's compressed contrast is retained.

translation.english_text: Are you going to carry out my order or not?
I shall carry it out—Manoharan must ask forgiveness.
Yes; and within half a second.

Half a second? Before even that! But do you know from whom I must ask forgiveness? After feeding to my sharp sword the murderous eyes—the cruel tongue—of this crooked-minded woman whom you praise as Komalavalli—the hessonite statue—the singing cuckoo—the leaping deer; after making corpses of you if you oppose it, and of that lady beside you if she comes to your aid; after sending to the cremation ground those who fan this sorceress... I must run to my mother, with a whirling sword and encircling fame, and say ‘I have done it’—and ask her forgiveness. Shall I carry out that order?...... Are you ready...? Are you ready?...
Why tremble? Ha... ha... ha! Purushothaman—a tiger in name; when he draws his sword, the world trembles. Is he the one afraid like this? Pity! Fingers that tested the sharpness of the spear are now delighting in the deceiver's finger. Eyes that inspected the battle camp are sunk in the sin of this snake-charmer's spectacle. A heart that dwelt on forts and battlements is finding coolness beneath the shadow of this little wall?....—

translation.english_text: Do not speak!
The town speaks... the world speaks!
Yes—that you are a whore's son.
notes: The source insult is translated directly rather than softened.

translation.english_text: Ah!
Why—are you stunned to hear it? I shall say it a thousand times: you are a whore's son!

Ha... Amma,
enough of your speech. Here! I shall tear that mouth to a hundred pieces.
[The chain snaps.]
notes: The source-attached chain-breaking cue remains inside the linked turn.

translation.english_text: Manohara!
No one interfere. Manoharan's fury will not even look to see who is good and who is bad. Let go of my raised hand.

Purushothama! You who see the world through the rolling eyes of a trickster! You who came as a stain in the line of warrior-kings who lived holding honour alone as the good life! Wise man who cannot tell a peacock from a monkey! Blind man who calls the cool moon a firebrand; my mother is the birthplace of love—the abode of righteousness—the form of compassion—the sacred embodiment of chastity—a flawless gem—gold whose fineness never diminishes! I shall tear apart the limbs of you who slandered her! I shall cut to pieces the body of the rogue who goaded you into this treacherous speech. If you have courage—if there is strength in your shoulders—take up your sword—take up your death! If you have no courage—if you have become a coward in the swaying laughter of this coquette—run from here! Run showing your back! Dust-wind that came to cover the glory of Purananuru—run showing your back! Black darkness that came to hide Kalingathu Parani—run until your heels strike your calves...... run... run... run wailing..... run crying Om at the top of your voice... What, is it shameful?
Tiny worm that abused my mother...
Why have you turned into a statue? Hey, royal idol: the devotee of vengeance has come to perform worship! Stand just so! Stand without moving! I shall scoop up the blood of this sorceress and perform abhishekam for you. I shall garland you with the nerves of this destroyer. You praise her teeth as a jasmine smile in your drunken infatuation! I shall pull out those teeth and offer them in worship to you! Sinner... look... look, great sinner who reviled a chaste wife! Look at the fate that befalls you and your cushioned-bed queen!

translation.english_text: [Coming in] Drop the sword!
notes: The source-attached entrance cue remains inside the linked utterance.

translation.english_text: Who are you?... (stunned) Amma! Amma! Why have you come here, Amma? Your pure feet must not touch this place where wickedness rules, Amma!
Manohara!
Wait a moment, Mother! [Looking at the king] Where are you trying to run? Stop.
Manohara! Do not forget yourself as well!
Amma, if you had heard the cruel words that rang through this royal hall about you just a moment ago, you would not speak like this. Stay here; I shall return.
Amma! No harm. For every drop of blood that falls from your sacred golden hand, these wicked people must answer.
Manohara! It was only me they insulted, was it not?
Leave me! Even if my mother stops me, I will not spare the man who insulted my mother.
Manohara! If it is true that you are my son, listen to what I say.
Amma.

First plunge the sword into this belly from which you were born, and then go to the Maharaja! Stand upon your mother's corpse and fight your father. Hmm... here is your mother... kill me. Then walk according to your principle... I am standing here.
notes: The mother’s-body/father-war challenge is retained without euphemism.

translation.english_text: Amma!...

I am not going to keep talking now. I had sworn that I would never go of my own accord to see the man I had vowed not to see; because of you I have been forced to see him, and now I must beg my own son before the assembly—an unbearable humiliation!
What do you ask me to do now, Amma?
Give me the sword like this!
Shall I ask forgiveness too?
Manohara! My jewel! Your mother was not born into a coward's family. She did not become the wife of a coward. She did not bear a coward as her son, my dear! Better to die than to ask forgiveness.
notes: The threefold coward/family-wife-son sequence is preserved.

translation.english_text: Yes; that is my decision too. This cruel man must not be left alive. Death sentence for Manoharan!

Ha! Amma!...
At least now give me permission, Amma. I shall crush these wretches and fling them away. Still patience, Amma?
Now is precisely the time for patience!
Then what of me?
You must die.
I must die? Your son Manoharan must die?
Yes! A fortune no one else can obtain: a father himself killing his son! And the mother nodding her head to it—my treasure, who on this earth could receive such royal fortune? Go, son—go to die!
notes: The bitterly ironic `royal fortune` refrain is preserved.

translation.english_text: Amma! Are you the one saying this?
Yes! The mother who bore you! I myself say it! Die!
Amma, to be parted from you?
I myself have found the courage to part from you.
Amma! Amma!
Be quiet! Satyaseelar! Arrange to carry Manoharan away—to the execution ground!

notes: The two quoted crowd cries remain one source-record-linked unit.

translation.english_text:
No one speak! He is my son—I shall deal with him as I wish! After the death sentence is carried out, even the funeral must take place outside this empire!
[Taking Manoharan's hand]
Son! If this is my last kiss, let our graves meet us next!
notes: The exile-even-in-burial and grave-meeting images are retained; the source-attached hand-taking cue remains inside the linked turn.

translation.english_text: Mama...... why, Mama, did you tear away the petals of the blooming rose... why, Mama, did you cut the green branch of the jasmine that had spread and grown... I followed him out of pure good love...... why, Mama, did you cast me into waves of suffering... tell me, Mama, is my life now only a desert?......... Is my heart only a dark room? Is there no deliverance at all, Mama?......
notes: Rose/jasmine/waves/desert/dark-room imagery is preserved as one sustained lament.

translation.english_text: There is no use stirring up a matter that is finished.

What matter is finished, Mama? The bond called father and son?...... Or the tie called husband and wife? Even if both are finished as far as you are concerned, think from where I stand; I am your enemy's daughter. The noble man who captured my heart is your son. Is it not a strange thing, Mama, to subject a man with a heart capable of drawing even an enemy to such cruelty—and that too when his wife is pregnant? Why did a princess of the Pandiyan country come to the Chola palace............ to become a lotus of sorrow...? To lose happiness? Tell me, Mama.

translation.english_text: The mother-in-law's lesson—exactly the same for the daughter-in-law!
I am speaking to my Mama...
Mama... to you the Maharaja is Mama... all this trouble came from that doubt, girl!
Fie... do not speak, whore...
notes: The source insult is translated directly.

translation.english_text: What did you say... whore who became wife to a whore's son... what did you say...
notes: The reciprocal insult is not softened.

translation.english_text: Ah... Vasantha Sena...
Queens of chastity—no dagger alone; even God cannot come near!...
notes: The taunting hyperbole is retained.

translation.english_text:
Vasanthi!...
[Looking at Vijaya]...
Sinner!... you tried to destroy my desires in half a second...
notes: The source-attached gaze cue remains inside the linked turn.

translation.english_text: A plot is being laid, Maharaja—to bring me down!...

Do not fear... I shall put an end to the plot...... Who is there?
[A guard comes.]
Together with Padmavathi, put Vijaya too in the underground prison... Hmm... let it be done...
notes: The source-attached guard entrance remains inside the linked turn.

translation.english_text: Mama...

source_locator.description: The palace.

translation.english_text: [The palace.]
Maharaja! The prince has escaped.
What?
Ah! Manoharan escaped?
Yes... someone loosened the bonds and saved him; we could not even see them with our eyes.
Disaster has begun to grow, Prabhu! Search the entire city; wherever that destroyer is, seize him and bring him here.
Hmm... go.

source_locator.description: The cave; Manoharan is there after being rescued.

translation.english_text: [The cave.]
Impossible, Amma... impossible... (looking around) What is this... I, who was killed, am alive...
Prince!
Who are you... who are you... Satyaseelar! Who is this man?
I shall tell you the details later... he is the one who saved you.

Saving me...... saving Manoharan... the king's wish... Mother's loving command.... fulfil them at once... kill me... kill me... kill me, Rajapriya! My beloved friend... you at least carry out my mother's command.
notes: The repeated kill-me cadence and contradictory king/mother commands remain explicit.

translation.english_text: Wait, Manohara!
Manohara... because a mother's word must not be broken, will you let the mother who sits in prison die abandoned?
Ah! Amma is in prison...
Not only Amma... Vijaya too...
Ah...
At least now understand...... why you must live.

source_locator.description: Underground prison; Padmavathi and Vijaya.

translation.english_text: [Underground prison. Padmavathi and Vijaya.]

The strong man who could guard his own life and the king's life with the point of his sword ended by fleeing and saving his life. All this ruin has come from your good intention, Athai! Where has he gone? How is he wandering now!
notes: The life/king's-life/sword contrast is preserved.

translation.english_text: Eat, Vijaya...
No, Athai!
A pregnant woman must not remain without eating. At least for the child growing in your womb, you have to eat... eat...
Athai... this gruel?...

source_locator.description: Vasantha Sena and Malini with fruit juice.

translation.english_text: [Vasantha Sena and Malini.]
It is wonderful...
This fruit juice will make the body shine...
I chose it knowing that, Malini! They say there was a beauty somewhere; to keep the sheen of her skin from fading, she would bathe in donkey's milk.
What wonder is this, Amma... if you asked, Purushothaman would bring even tiger's milk...
notes: The donkey-milk/tiger-milk comic escalation is preserved.

translation.english_text: What doubt is there about that, girl?
Leave that... why are you being so careless... Manoharan has escaped too. Shouldn't Vasanthan's coronation be conducted quickly?

What great task is that, girl? I am the king's very Veda-book. If I say the moon is the sun, he is bound to believe it... do not worry! With one flick of my eye, Vasanthan's coronation will be finished!
notes: The `king's Veda-book`, moon/sun and eye-flick boasting images are retained.

source_locator.description: The physician, Vikatan and Vasanthan rehearse a mock durbar/coronation.

translation.english_text: [The physician, Vikatan and Vasanthan begin a mock durbar rehearsal.]
King of kings... Raja Marthanda...
notes: The mock royal honorific chain is retained rather than normalized into one generic title.

translation.english_text: Royal majesty... royal splendour...
Royal valour, courage, prowess...
Hero of the battlefield, brave warrior, champion...
Great King Vasantha who drinks thin gruel without salt—paraak! paraak!
notes: The lofty titles collapse into the saltless-gruel punchline; ceremonial `பராக்` is retained as `paraak`.

translation.english_text: Thom... thom... we came......
notes: The rhythmic nonsense is retained.

translation.english_text: Vasantha! Look here... Amma will scold us, get up... it must look like a real durbar... you must do as I say... hmm... sit here, Maharaja!

source_locator.description: The source prints only `:` before this instruction following Vikatan's setup.

translation.english_text: Now you must say exactly as I tell you......
notes: No speaker is invented for the source-empty field.

translation.english_text: Now who are you?
Now who are you?
notes: Vasanthan parrots the prompt exactly, preserving the joke.

translation.english_text: Tch... answer me...
Tch... answer me...
Oh dear... answer me, Maharaja?
Oh dear... answer me, Maharaja!
You're supposed to answer ‘Maharaja’!
Hmm... all right... all right... Maharaja!
Ah... I am the minister!
Hmm...
And he is—(pointing to the physician)
I know... I know...... Maharani...... come... come... sit...
Maharaja... he is the commander...... now who is the Maharani?
There... we can make Malini the queen... come...
(To Malini) Listen to me just a little... only for today you are Maharani... go and sit with the Maharaja...
[Grinning]... Shabash....
Next, if a king from another country comes happily, you must speak happily; if he comes angrily, you must speak angrily...
All right!... Minister!...
Hmm—the durbar may begin....
Commander! Let the dance begin...
Tell the Maharani to dance...
Yes, O king! Look, there is no one else... so let her dance!
Hmm... dance! In our country everyone is equal... everyone may dance... women who do not know how to dance are not women at all! Isn't that right, Vikata?
notes: The comic pseudo-egalitarian proclamation is preserved as printed.

translation.english_text: The way women walk these days is itself like a dance, isn't it!

source_locator.description: Purushothaman enters during the mock durbar.

translation.english_text: [Purushothaman enters.]
Oh-ho! A king from the neighbouring country?... Have you come happily? Have you come angrily?...
Enough, man... keep quiet...

Oh! He has come angrily... Hey!... brainless king!... foolish ruler!... where have you come? State the business that brought you... why have you come to Vasanthan's durbar?... Minister!... Is that enough anger!...
notes: Vasanthan follows Vikatan's instruction literally and insults the real king; the comic escalation is retained.

translation.english_text: Hey, Vikata, what performance is this!...
A coronation rehearsal... Amma asked us to show it!...
Physician! What medicine are you giving him—are you curing his madness or not!...
Madness?... who said that? This is an incurable disease!...
notes: The joke explicitly loops back to scene 28's diagnosis.

source_locator.description: The mock durbar breaks off under the king's arrival.

translation.english_text: [The mock durbar breaks off.]

source_locator.description: Garden.

translation.english_text: [Garden.]
You have come, Swami? I was waiting on the garden rock—you have come by way of the palace.
What does it matter which path... does the light change in your speech, in your honeyed eyes, Vasanthi!
notes: The speech/eyes/light image is retained.

translation.english_text: How could it change—Ahalya created for Indra—Tara created for Chandra—Vasantha created for Purushothaman—
notes: The mythological three-part self-comparison is retained without explanatory substitution.

translation.english_text: Vasanthi! My dear... I do not even know what to say to you—
Remain mute—I enjoy that elegance...
Now... whatever you ask, I shall give—
There comes the danger!... Even what I had thought of asking, I am not going to ask now...
Why, Vasanthi!...
You will say, ‘The adventuress waited for the right moment to ask.’ Am I Kaikeyi who deceived Dasaratha?... No... no...
notes: Kaikeyi/Dasaratha remain explicit cultural references.

translation.english_text: What is it, Vasanthi? Ask!...
No... hmm!...
All right... I am going...
Ayyo!... my life will leave me—sit down.
Then... tell me...
Manoharan has left the country...
Why stir that up...
No... a country without a prince... is like a painting without beauty!...
What can be done about that...
Why, if we made our Vasanthan prince...
Madness! You are even madder than Vasanthan!...
Swami...
He must not be made prince!... A madman should be crowned a prophet—if we crown him.... first you will be mad—then I will be mad—after that this whole country will be mad...
notes: The mad-you/mad-me/mad-country escalation is retained.

translation.english_text: Enough... enough!... do not describe it—King Vasantha deserves this and still more. I thought you were wise... [angrily] you are a void of wisdom!
notes: `ஞான சூன்யம்` is kept close to its literal `void of wisdom` insult.

translation.english_text: (Cunningly) Call me a fool three thousand times—I'd be happy!... But... only do not think your Vasanthi a deceiver... Swami!... I merely asked you for an idea—he is not only my son—he is your son too—what desire can I have beyond yours! My aim is your happiness... not self-interest...
notes: The sudden anger-to-cunning reversal remains visible.

translation.english_text: Don't I know that, my dear! But Vasanthan!
No more of that talk—dangerous talk!... I too know what will happen if madness is crowned... I was teasing you. And you, before I could finish.... Hmm!
Vasanthi!...
Prabhu!... the moon-terrace is seeking us—come...

‘There is no profit now in trusting Purushothaman—I must make a new plan. This ungrateful king must be exiled from the country... Manoharan must be killed... Vasanthan must be crowned. The one man who can help in all this is my old lover Ugrasenan.’
notes: The exact source label marks this as Vasantha Sena's inner thought; it is not converted to external speech.

source_locator.description: Vasantha Sena goes into the room; Vasanthan follows.

translation.english_text: Vasantha Sena goes into the room. Vasanthan follows.

source_locator.description: Vasantha Sena writes a letter; the invisible figure follows; she trembles.

translation.english_text: [Vasantha Sena writes a letter. The invisible figure follows. Vasantha Sena trembles.]
Who's there! A wicked man is hiding inside. Do not let him go!

source_locator.description: The invisible figure calls Vasanthan.

translation.english_text: [The invisible figure calls Vasanthan.]
Are you a ghost? A god?
No, Vasantha... I am a human being.
A human? I can't see you with my eyes.
You will not see me! It is the fruit of the grace and knowledge of my lord Gurunathar. The work of a medicine.
Will you give me a little of that medicine?
I will! But you must listen and do as I say.
First call a soldier to come...

source_locator.description: Vikatan calls a soldier; the invisible figure ties him up and slips away.

translation.english_text: [Vikatan calls a soldier. The invisible figure ties him up and slips away.]

source_locator.description: Vasantha Sena writes the letter and places it inside the container/cage as printed.

translation.english_text: [Vasantha Sena writes the letter and places it inside the container.]
notes: The English does not reconstruct or normalize the source object's wording beyond the verified scene action.

source_locator.description: Cave.

translation.english_text: [Cave.]
The vengeful woman has prepared the palm-leaf letter. To make her plan succeed, if we are careless even a little with this final letter, it itself will become our death-letter!
notes: The `letter/death-letter` wordplay is retained.

translation.english_text: Tell us the matter, Varma!
The deceiver tried to crown Vasanthan! The king refused. So she has sent a letter to the outsider Ugrasenan, asking him to seize this palace and make her son king.
Ugrasenan! King of Imayapuri!
Yes! The man who has been waiting for a chance to enter our empire.
The man bringing a reply from Ugrasenan must come by this very route. Come, let us see.

source_locator.description: Akshayan comes on horseback; Manoharan stops him.

translation.english_text: [Akshayan comes on horseback. Manoharan stops him.]
Who are you!
Are you asking me? I am myself!
notes: The evasive comic tautology is retained.

translation.english_text: Where are you going?
To the place I must go!

source_locator.description: Manoharan and Rajapriyan attack Akshayan, bind him to a stone pillar, and take a letter from him.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan and Rajapriyan attack Akshayan and bind him to a stone pillar. Manoharan takes a letter from him.]

source_locator.description: Ugrasenan's letter to Vasantha Sena printed in full on PDF 65.

translation.english_text:
‘Dear Vasantha Sena!

Keep Akshayan as your aide and attend to what must be done inside the palace. The troops and I are setting out. We shall do away with Purushothaman. We shall begin a new life.

Ugrasenan.’
notes: The salutation, body and signature are preserved as one printed-letter unit; no words are supplied beyond the source.

translation.english_text: Treason... we must not let this go!
Let us set out now... that crooked-minded woman must be destroyed root and branch.
notes: `கூண்டோடு அழிக்க` is rendered as total/root-and-branch destruction without adding a literal cage not warranted in this idiomatic context.

translation.english_text: If you destroy her, your valour will be revealed. That whore's disguise will not be revealed. Prince! Have I wandered yearning all this time merely to kill her in half a second? I too could do that; I would have done it long ago.
notes: The valour/disguise contrast is retained.

translation.english_text: Why did you not?

Wisdom, Prince! Wisdom. Had I killed her then, the king—who had lost his eyes for that deceitful woman—would have shed tears for her. Her schemes would not have been exposed. The world could not have known her deceits. Our cleverness does not lie in killing her. It lies in exposing her plots.
notes: The repeated `விவேகம்` and killing-versus-exposing contrast are preserved.

translation.english_text: And the way to do that......
Just as a thorn is removed with another thorn, a plot must be defeated by a plot. I shall tell you—come.
notes: The thorn-with-thorn proverb is translated literally rather than replaced by an English proverb.

source_locator.description: King's palace.

translation.english_text: [King's palace.]
Maharaja...... there is a man said to be a great expert at treating madness...
Is that so!... Take him to Vasanthi!......
Your command!......

source_locator.description: In Vasantha Sena's inner quarters, the guard points out Manoharan disguised as Akshayan.

translation.english_text: [In Vasantha Sena's inner quarters, the guard points out Manoharan, who is in Akshayan's guise.]
Amma—Maharaja sent this man to you. They say he is a great physician...
I am a physician. My name is..... Ugrasenan's messenger... [understanding]
notes: The source-attached `புரிந்துகொண்டு` cue is retained without assigning an unstated subject.

translation.english_text: A long name...

source_locator.description: Manoharan extends the letter to Vasantha Sena; she reads it.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan extends the letter to Vasantha Sena. She reads it.]

source_locator.description: The source prints `உமது பெயர்?` without a speaker label after the letter-reading action.

translation.english_text: Your name?
notes: No speaker is inferred because the source line has no printed speaker label.

translation.english_text: Akshayan!
You have fooled the king properly.
Yes—no one can discover who I am...
All right... keep acting just like a physician—I'll attend to the rest.
Acting? That's easy!... Oh!...
notes: The boast in `நடிப்பதா பிரமாதம்` is kept brisk rather than formalized.

translation.english_text: Hey, physician... medicine, medicine—you keep taking my life!
notes: The literal `உயிரை வாங்குறே` sets up the physician's death-joke in the next exchange and is retained.

translation.english_text: That's exactly what I'm trying to do, but it isn't happening!
notes: The physician's reply preserves the dark comic reversal of `உயிரை வாங்க`.

translation.english_text: What for? To take my life?
Tch...tch... by God's grace, may your lifespan go on... this disease go on... and this humble servant's job go on; I am forever praying to Yama-Dharma for it.
notes: The threefold `நீடிச்சு` repetition and the joke of praying to Yama-Dharma are preserved.

translation.english_text: Physician! What is Yama's vehicle?
A buffalo bull! That's why he comes so slowly to all the bad people...
notes: The Yama/buffalo joke is retained directly.

translation.english_text: Yes... no doubt... no doubt—
Physician... first, allow me to convey my deepest condolences...
What is it, Vikatare...
Life is impermanent... here... a new physician has arrived for Vasanthan!
notes: The mock-condolence setup in `நிலையில்லா வாழ்வு` is kept intact.

translation.english_text: Then I...
Step aside a little, my boy...

source_locator.description: Manoharan enters in Akshayan's guise.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan enters in Akshayan's guise.]
Hey, new physician... what all do you know?
Without even giving medicine, I'll put an end to the disease!
notes: The ominous joke in `ஒரு முடிவு கட்டுவேன்` is left intact.

translation.english_text: Then... you're the new physician, no doubt... hey, old physician, you run...
notes: Vasanthan's recurring `சந்தேகமில்லே` refrain is retained as `no doubt`.

source_locator.description: Ugrasenan's tent.

translation.english_text: [Ugrasenan's tent.]
Veerasimha! We may have to set out suddenly... all our soldiers are ready, aren't they!
Ready, my king!
(Handing over a palm-leaf letter) Enter Purushothaman's palace and, through Vasantha Sena, get this delivered to Akshayan.
notes: The source-attached letter-handover action remains inside the linked utterance.

translation.english_text: They say Ugrasenan has arrived; they say they're all coming disguised as sadhus...
Sadhus... disguise...
What, Akshaya?
Nothing, Amma. Many empires have fallen under the guise of sadhus...
notes: The political irony of `சாது வேடத்தில்` is retained rather than softened.

translation.english_text: Oh! Yes... how do we bring them into the palace?
We shall have to think it over...
What is there to think about? I'll arrange it in half a second.

source_locator.description: Ugrasenan's sadhu group is welcomed with music and devotional cries; the king and Vasanthi receive and honour them with devotion and respect.

translation.english_text: [Ugrasenan's group of sadhus is welcomed with drums, music and devotional cries...... The king and Vasanthi receive and honour the group with devotion, reverence and respect......]
Welcome...... welcome...... I am blessed.
May Bhagavan's great grace be attained... King Purushothaman... the world itself is a drama; who knows what will happen tomorrow!......
notes: The disguised holy-man register and `the world is a drama` aphoristic turn are preserved.

translation.english_text: True, true!......
So this is the queen!......
(Nods his head)......
notes: The source stores this action under an explicit speaker label; it remains linked as dialogue-kind rather than being silently reclassified.

translation.english_text: Mahalakshmi!... Nalayini of the Kali age... Queen...... may you live as your heart desires!... may your thoughts be fulfilled......
notes: `மகாலஷ்மி` and `கலிகால நளாயினி` remain culturally explicit rather than being replaced with generic praise.

translation.english_text: Vasantha... bow to Swami!
May I have the company of those noble ones who, with singleness of mind, think upon Your sacred flower-feet... Vikata, I've forgotten the lesson, da...
notes: The half-remembered devotional recitation is kept elevated before Vasanthan breaks it with his comic admission.

translation.english_text: Enough... enough.
Long live! Long live...... Hey, King... I have come at just the right time. A great danger is waiting for you........
Swami!......
If you are to escape that danger, you and your queen must remain apart from this very moment until tomorrow morning.
Is that so?
Otherwise, death will occur...
Be separated from Maharaja?......
Only until tomorrow morning, Vasanthi!...
Hmm—separate... separate...
I remember now: may I not mingle in the company of those who keep one thing within and speak another without.
notes: The devotional-lesson cadence is retained as part of Vasanthan's comic recitation.

translation.english_text: Vasantha
Forgetfulness... desire for women must be forgotten.
notes: The source prints `மறவு பெண்ணாசை மறக்கவேண்டும்`; it is preserved as printed rather than silently normalized to a familiar devotional line.

translation.english_text: Hey! Keep quiet!
Wisdom is needed...
Vasantha!

source_locator.description: Vasanthi leaves.

translation.english_text: [Vasanthi leaves]...
notes: The source's unusual agreement is not used to infer or alter identity; the English avoids adding a gendered pronoun.

translation.english_text: Everything is God's doing! King!... this body needs a little rest...
notes: The counterfeit ascetic register remains visible in `this body` rather than being normalized to `I`.

translation.english_text: I'll arrange it at once......

source_locator.description: The king leaves; Ugrasenan's soldiers disguised as sadhus spread through the palace, kill the guards and occupy their places.

translation.english_text: [The king leaves. Ugrasenan's soldiers, disguised as sadhus, spread throughout the palace, kill the guards and occupy their places.]

source_locator.description: Cave.

translation.english_text: [Cave.]

Saffron robes! Beneath them, an army bearing knives has poured in as though a sluice had been opened... in the guise of ascetics, without a single barrier! If we delay even half a moment now, the Chola realm will become enslaved. Set out at once.
notes: `காஷாய உடை`, the knife-bearing army, and the opened-sluice image are all retained rather than compressed into a generic infiltration summary.

translation.english_text: Yes, that is right! We must not let this go. Set out immediately.

Wait. We have the strength of mind to free our motherland! At the same time, we must think a little about the strength of the enemy's army too. Let us send Rajapriyan at once to the Pandiyan country. Once the Pandiyan forces arrive, we shall begin our struggle!
notes: The contrast between `மன வலிமை` and the enemy's `படை வலிமை` is kept visible.

translation.english_text: Good idea! Prince! You must enter the palace at once. Only then can you keep watch so that no danger approaches your mother, father or wife. We shall take care of the rest!
Manohara! You set out at once. Rajapriya, you leave immediately for the Pandiyan country!

source_locator.description: Puja room.

translation.english_text: [Puja room.]
Who is it—oh... Queen Vasantha Devi?
Are Swami's thoughts on God?
notes: This sets up the `ஆண்டவன் / ஆண்டு கொண்டிருப்பவன்` wordplay in Ugrasenan's reply.

translation.english_text: Not about the Lord. About the one who is ruling... sit down, my delight.
notes: The Lord/ruler turn in `ஆண்டவன் / ஆண்டு கொண்டிருப்பவன்` is retained rather than flattened.

translation.english_text: Have some fruit juice.
First I shall drink the nectar of your gaze, my dear!
notes: The source's `பார்வை ரசம்` image is preserved as gaze-nectar rather than reduced to ordinary flirtation.

translation.english_text: How many days it has been since I saw you.
Did you call me, Amma?
No, go away.
(Running his hand through her hair) Ah! A gathering of clouds. (Showing her teeth) A jasmine garden. (Stroking her cheek) A field of roses!
notes: The cloud / jasmine-garden / rose-field sequence and its source-attached gestures are retained in order.

translation.english_text: Swami!
Altogether, the very limit of delight!
Yes... how have you planned all the plans?
notes: The source's repetition of `திட்டங்கள் / திட்டியிருக்கிறீர்கள்` remains audible.

translation.english_text: Splendidly! All the important parts of the palace are being occupied by our warriors disguised as mendicants. One command from us is enough—war! Purushothaman under arrest!
notes: The abrupt `போர்! புருஷோத்தமன் கைது!` military cadence is preserved.

translation.english_text: Even war will not be necessary. I have Purushothaman's soldiers in the palm of my hand.
notes: `என் கைக்குள் போட்டு வைத்திருக்கிறேன்` remains a control-in-the-hand image rather than being generalized.

translation.english_text: Sabash! What if war does come? Once enemy troops have entered the palace, who can resist and win?
Have the enemy troops come only into the palace?
notes: The line deliberately opens the sexual double meaning that follows.

translation.english_text: You mean they have come all the way into the inner chambers? This is not to fight. To surrender.
notes: The palace/inner-chambers and fight/surrender double entendre is preserved without explanatory expansion.

translation.english_text: I will come tonight.
notes: The concise closing line is left to carry its source double meaning without added explanation.

source_locator.description: Corridor of the prison.

translation.english_text: [Corridor of the prison.]
Hey, don't go that way... Vijaya Amma... she's in labour pains...
notes: The guard's colloquial register is retained.

source_locator.description: The source prints `ஆள்......அப்படியா......` without a speaker delimiter after the guard's line.

translation.english_text: Man...... is that so......
notes: `ஆள்` remains inside the translated source text rather than being promoted to an inferred speaker label.

source_locator.description: Inside the prison.

translation.english_text: (Inside the prison.)

(Bending over the child) O treasure of my treasures! You who should have slept in a diamond-studded cradle, listening to Tamil music from a thousand nursemaids—I never even imagined you would be rolling here in a straw-filled pen...
notes: The thousand nursemaids / Tamil music / diamond cradle versus straw-filled enclosure contrast is retained in full.

translation.english_text: Atthe!......
notes: The kinship address is retained rather than flattened to a generic English address.

translation.english_text: My dear... daughter of the Pandiyan king...... did you come as my daughter-in-law to suffer like this......
Only after I came, Atthe, have so many torments come upon you and your beloved son...... all of it only after this sinner set foot here........
notes: Vijaya's self-blaming `பாவி` is retained rather than softened.

translation.english_text: Vijaya!... No, child... wherever your flower-feet touch, even earth turns to gold... you are not the one who turned the golden mansion into a mound of dust... she lives in bliss......
notes: The flower-feet / earth-to-gold and golden-mansion / dust-mound contrasts are preserved.

source_locator.description: Puja room.

translation.english_text: [Puja room.]
How are the grapes?
Everything your fingers touch turns sweet.
This guava is still inferior to the taste of my lips, isn't it?
notes: The sensual comparison is retained.

translation.english_text: What lie is there in that?
notes: The source `கொய்யா / பொய்யா` guava/lie sound-play is kept as far as English allows.

translation.english_text: My love, how many days has it been since we enjoyed this bliss?
I yearned and pined, wondering when I would see you again, slender-bangled one!
notes: `ஏந்திழையே` is retained as a heightened poetic address rather than flattened.

translation.english_text: Swami!
Vasanthi!
Prabho! Where are we now?
We are on our way to heaven, my dear!

source_locator.description: Outside the window of the puja room.

translation.english_text: [Outside the window of the puja room.]
Physician! Physician! Physician!
What?
Mother and the holy man are going off to heaven! Come! Come! Let us go and save Mother.
You go and bring the Maharaja at once!
Ah! That's right... no doubt! No doubt.

source_locator.description: The king's chamber.

translation.english_text: [The king's chamber.]
Father! Father!
What is this, da?
They say Mother and the holy man are going to heaven!
Come, Father...... come......

source_locator.description: Puja room.

translation.english_text: [Puja room.]
Why so many lamps, Vasanthi?
Why? Would one lamp be enough?
Even that is unnecessary when you, the lamp that never goes out, are beside me!

source_locator.description: The king pounds on the door; Ugrasenan draws his sword.

translation.english_text: [The king pounds on the door. Ugrasenan draws his sword.]
No! The whole affair will be ruined. I will handle it. Come this way... [She sends him into a room and closes the door; the door breaks.] Who is it?
notes: Source-attached action remains inside the linked utterance.

translation.english_text: Who?...... Wretch!
Ah! Prabhu! Did you not say you must not see this servant? It was the Lord's command!
What Lord's command, woman? What? At dead midnight, upon a hamsa-down couch, with that male—with that fellow, was it the Lord's command that you should conduct a revel of pleasure?
notes: The physical page-break interruption after `ஆண்—` is preserved in page segments.

english_page_segments.english_text: What Lord's command, woman? What? At dead midnight, upon a hamsa-down couch, with that male—
with that fellow, was it the Lord's command that you should conduct a revel of pleasure?

translation.english_text: Ah! What the eye sees is false! What the ear hears is false! Only thorough inquiry is truth, Maharaja!
notes: The proverbial three-part cadence is preserved.

translation.english_text: Chi! Do not put on a drama! Where is that mendicant?
He is in the realm of dhyana.
notes: `தியான லோகம்` is kept as a devotional-register phrase.

translation.english_text: In the realm of udyana, is he? You town-ruining wretch! You can no longer deceive Purushothaman.
notes: The source's `தியான / உத்தியான` sound-play is kept visible as dhyana/udyana.

translation.english_text: Maharaja! Think calmly. Do not slander Amma. She is a virtuous woman!

You who have come to lecture me on the marks of a virtuous woman—embodiment of treachery that betrays the house whose food you ate! All this came because of you. You screamed, ‘She is about to die...... come at once and save her!’ You cast a stain upon the noble Satyaseelar and the chaste Padmavathi. I did not know then that you were the crowbar in this thief-woman's hand!
notes: The house-betrayal and `கன்னக்கோல்` burglary image are retained.

translation.english_text: Maharaja!
Tell the truth. Is it not true that you and this destroyer lived by deceiving me? Speak, woman! Speak!
Do nothing to her. I will tell you everything myself. I poisoned my husband and killed him. I fabricated the story that spotless Padmavathi had lost her chastity.
Ah!
What, da! Are you wondering why I am telling every truth? I say all this not to obtain your forgiveness. I say it with the courage of knowing that from now on you can do nothing to me!
Deceiver!

Deceiver! I am the deceiver? For so many years you kept me merely as a lotus of the bedchamber, and you are the one who levelled to the ground even my one unquenchable desire—that my boy should be crowned! Are you not the deceiver?
notes: `பள்ளியறைப் பதுமை` remains an elevated bedchamber-lotus image.

translation.english_text: Your boy's coronation—forget it! No one can wrest this land from the line of Purushothaman.
You are dreaming! Prepare the address of felicitation—for Vasanthan's coronation! For the coronation of Vasanthan, son of Kesari Varman—
Stop it, woman! Stop, whore!
Poor man! Have you understood that only now?
Sinner! Harlot! If I leave you alive, you will keep raving. Who is there? Run here! Seize her!

source_locator.description: The guards stand without moving.

translation.english_text: [The guards stand without moving.]
It will not happen. Your authority has set. These are my warriors! Akshaya, arrest him!
notes: The source's sunset image for vanished authority is retained.

translation.english_text: Ah! You are ordering my arrest?
Yes—you. I order you arrested. And in this, your last royal dress! Akshaya! Why are you standing there, Akshaya? Hmm............ let it proceed.......

source_locator.description: Manoharan arrests his father.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan arrests his father.]

[To himself] Purushothama! You have ground into dust the fame of a lineage that never knew how to show its back! A beast—with fetters locked upon those hands that bore the sword! O land of valour! Will you not forgive me?
notes: The `விலங்கு` beast/fetter word-play is carried into the line as far as English allows.

source_locator.description: Prison chamber.

translation.english_text: [Prison chamber.]
At a mere nod of his head, petty kings would bow with tribute and army commanders would rise roaring. Today the majesty of that lion of the sceptre has been confined behind prison bars.
Cowards! Is there not even one warrior loyal to the king here?
There are. Every one of them is in prison. Without a drop of blood being spent, without the clang of swords being heard, our sovereign has beaten the drum of victory.
Sovereign! Even an ascetic who does not know how to hold a spear, who entered the battlefield bearing a kamandalam, is called a sovereign!
notes: The spear/kamandalam contrast is preserved.

translation.english_text: Not so! Ugrasenan is clever! He understood that to oppose Purushothaman in the bedchamber he needed neither arrows nor shields. So he decided that saffron robes and kamandalams would be enough.
Enough, da—stop. My valour has not become worthless merely because I fell into the net cast by a whore.
Who is a whore? Vasantha Sena is a chaste woman! Ten-and-a-half-touch gold.
notes: `பத்தரை மாற்று தங்கம்` is retained as a period purity metaphor rather than replaced by a modern carat figure.

translation.english_text: No! It is my ten-and-a-half-touch gold whom I threw into the underground prison! Sinner that I am! Padmavathi! You are the ten-and-a-half-touch gold. The wretch who accused you has received his proper reward. Padmavathi!
Grieving is useless. Tomorrow morning Vasanthan will be crowned.

Vasanthan! That deceitful woman's son—the twisted-brained one—the future guardian of our prosperous land! Alas! Manohara! My treasure born to rule! The Chandala who drove you to death has received his proper punishment. Manohara! To you, to your mother, to my jewel Vijaya, how many obstacles I placed! From whom shall I ask forgiveness for all of it? Where are you, Manohara! Though I had committed a thousand crimes, if danger came to your father you would run here ready to give your very head! Who will tell you this news, Manohara! Manohara, where are you, Manohara!
notes: The repeated invocations of Manoharan and the father's escalating remorse are preserved.
Physical source word-split across PDF 75→76 is represented in English page segments.

translation.english_text: I am right here!
Where? Where is my Manoharan? Where is Manoharan? Manohara! Manohara!

source_locator.description: Palace.

translation.english_text: [Palace.]
Akshaya! They say Vijaya, who is lying in the underground prison, has given birth to a child.
Ah!
What is it, Akshaya?
Nothing...... nothing. A bud has sprouted at the very moment of destruction!
Yes. You must pluck out that very bud and cast it away!
Ah! What—me?
Who is there but you to do this deed? Here! Go this very moment!

source_locator.description: Vasantha Sena gives him the signet ring.

translation.english_text: [She gives him the signet ring.]

I must kill my own treasure.
No... no...
notes: The source-unlabelled `இல்ல...இல்ல...` continuation remains inside the preceding explicit Manoharan record, matching the immutable dialogue layer.

source_locator.description: Manoharan draws his sword.

translation.english_text: [He draws his sword.]

Manohara, stop. Do not give way to fury; do not become a slave to haste! The palace is full of enemies. Your mother is in prison—your father is suffering. You rush forward with sword outstretched... who will protect your unfading flowers? Who will protect your many-coloured parrots?
notes: The inner voice and the paired `unfading flowers / coloured parrots` protective images are retained.

source_locator.description: Manoharan turns back and goes to the prison.

translation.english_text: [He turns back and goes to the prison.]

source_locator.description: The real Akshayan cuts the ropes binding him to the stone pillar near the cave.

translation.english_text: [Near the cave, the real Akshayan—who was tied to a stone pillar—struggles and cuts through the ropes.]

source_locator.description: Palace.

translation.english_text: [Palace.]
Let us discuss what must be done tomorrow.
What more remains to be done?
Tomorrow is Vasanthan's coronation.
Certainly. But before that, we must proclaim that the country is under our control.
Will proclaiming it bring any danger?
Danger!... From whom? Is there anyone in this world capable of opposing me?
In this flood of triumph, do not forget that Manoharan is still alive!

source_locator.description: Prison; Manoharan enters by showing the signet ring.

translation.english_text: [Prison. Showing the signet ring, Manoharan enters.]
Mother.
Who are you!
Manoharan... sent me!
Manoharan... is my jewel well?
Atthai! Where do they say he is?
Where else could he be, when he is always in your heart?
Who are you, son?
I will tell you that later. Now both of you must escape from here.
What?
Yes! Manoharan's secret arrangement. Here is the signet ring. You can leave without fear and without anyone stopping you. Set out.
To escape by trickery—no, I cannot. I cannot disobey the Maharaja's order. Tell Manoharan that.
notes: The source's anomalous comma delimiter after `பத்` remains source metadata in the immutable dialogue layer; translation does not normalize it.

translation.english_text: Atthai!

source_locator.description: Colon-only source line after Vijaya's `Atthai!`; no printed speaker label.

translation.english_text: Tell Manoharan, thambi—I have a precious grandson, born here in prison!
notes: The source begins with an empty speaker field; no speaker is inferred. `தம்பி` is retained as the vocative `thambi`.

translation.english_text: I am telling you to leave only to avert the great danger coming upon this grandson.
For the queen herself to disobey the king's command...? It would not be proper.
Then... Princess! At least give me that child. I will carry him away.
Ah! The child?
If the child's life is to be saved......?
Atthai, do not trust him...... some plot is under way to kill the child.
Impossible... impossible... go away.

source_locator.description: Palace.

translation.english_text: [Palace.]
Maharaja! Akshayan has come. He says he wishes to see you.
He has come?... Tell him to come here.

source_locator.description: Colon-only line following Vasantha Sena's order to admit Akshayan.

translation.english_text: He must have come with news of victory. He must have killed Vijaya's child and returned. This reward is for him.
notes: Empty source speaker field; no speaker is inferred.

source_locator.description: Second consecutive colon-only source line.

translation.english_text: Your commander is very cunning.
notes: Empty source speaker field; no speaker is inferred.

translation.english_text: What doubt is there about that? Oh... come... Akshaya, come...

source_locator.description: Colon-only question immediately before the real Akshayan enters.

translation.english_text: What is it, Akshaya?
notes: Empty source speaker field; no speaker is inferred.

source_locator.description: The real Akshayan enters.

translation.english_text: [The real Akshayan enters.]
Who is he? Akshayan?
Yes.
Ah! No.
I am the real Akshayan. The one who deceived you all this while was a false Akshayan, madam!
notes: The source semicolon delimiter is preserved in the immutable record; translation does not regularize it.

source_locator.description: Colon-only continuation after the real Akshayan identifies himself.

translation.english_text: Yes... Maharaja! They tied me up. I have only just escaped and come.
notes: Empty source speaker field; no speaker is inferred even though context strongly suggests Akshayan.

translation.english_text: They tied you up? Who?
Manoharan!
notes: The source semicolon delimiter remains source metadata and is not silently normalized.

translation.english_text: Ah! Manoharan! Then the Akshayan who is here?
notes: The source semicolon delimiter remains source metadata and is not silently normalized.

translation.english_text: Manoharan!
Where is he......
He has gone to the prison.
We must not let him go.

source_locator.description: Prison.

translation.english_text: [Prison.]
Come! Let me hold that child for a little while!

translation.english_text: May I not give even one kiss to Manoharan's child?

Mother... Father, who has understood the truth, longs to see you and me. Thinking again and again of the cruelties now past, he sheds tears. He is shaken and tormented... shaken and tormented, Mother... Mother... Mother...
The Maharaja has understood the truth! My crowned lord has understood the truth. He has understood the truth.

translation.english_text: Atthai!... What is it, Atthai!
The darkness has lifted. Joy is dawning.
Joy...! For us?... In this condition?

source_locator.description: Manoharan is tied to a pillar.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan is tied to a pillar.]
Manohara! Everyone has been able to bind only your body; they could not bind your life. Very soon it will gain its freedom and go to another world!
Mother! [Ugrasenan strikes him.]
Mother!
Hmm! Ayyo, pity—this babbling child is calling for his mother.
Mother!
Pitiful creature! Why call your mother until your mouth aches? Wait a little! I shall send you to the very otherworld where your grandmother is.
No. First the child! Then Manoharan! His own jewel must be killed right before his eyes. Nurse! Go! Bring the child;

source_locator.description: Vasanthan enters.

translation.english_text: [Vasanthan enters.]
Anna, what is this? Who tied you up?
Vasantha...
Come here.
No... all this is your doing, isn't it! Mother... untie Anna! Hmm!
Vasantha... keep quiet. You know nothing.
I know everything. You put my beloved father, Periyamma and Anni all in prison; then you tied Anna too and started beating him. I cannot allow this.
Anna...
Vasantha...
Vasantha, come this way.

Anna, break all those chains...... let me go, Mother!

[She drags him into a room.]

Let me go... let me go.
notes: The source-unlabelled continuation after the dragging action remains inside the preceding explicit Vasanthan record.

translation.english_text: Keep quiet. I am doing everything only for your good.
Ah! Tying up Anna and killing him—is that for the younger brother's good?
My dear, don't you want to be king?
King? No! No. Then some queen will come to you and throw you in prison! Let me die if I must. I don't want that throne, Mother!
It is all my fate! Of all things, you had to be born from my womb!
That's exactly what I worry about too.
Shut your mouth.
I can't.
You can't?
Mother! Mother! [She shuts the door and leaves.]

What crime has this tiny infant committed, son? This child has committed no crime! No crime at all except being born into a world where the cruel roam!
We know nothing about all that. The Maharani's order!

Who is the Maharani outside there! Who are you to ask for my child? Tell that wretch—the princess of the Pandya country refuses to hand over the tender creeper she herself bore. If she has courage, tell her to fight me face to face and take the child!
notes: `பைங்கொடி` is retained as the tender-creeper image for the child.

translation.english_text: Vijaya, be patient!

Atthai! Are you asking me to hand my child over to that murderess, Atthai? Even hens fight the hawk circling to kill their chicks! Am I a woman with less feeling of motherhood than they? Tell them to kill me. After my life is gone, let them take away my living portrait.
notes: The hen/hawk maternal image and `ஜீவ ஓவியம்` living-portrait image are preserved.

translation.english_text: Yes. The opportunity has fallen into our hands by itself. Vasanthan is fortunate.

The young breeze of the Chola Empire—poor tender infant. For the sins of the father, this bud is going to die. Manohara! Look once upon the beautiful face of your child. Gather upon your lips all the longing you have held down, and give your child's tender cheek one last kiss.

[He stretches the child toward Manoharan, taunting him.]

source_locator.description: Manoharan is shaken; the child smiles without understanding.

translation.english_text: [Manoharan is shaken; the child, knowing nothing, smiles.]

Hmm, you are smiling—poor thing, smile well. Born crying, you will die smiling. Is it not Pandya blood and Chola blood that run surging through your body? Perhaps that is why, with such joy, you will sleep in the cradle of death.
Quickly! [Ugrasenan raises his sword over the child.]
notes: Source-attached action remains within the labelled turn.

translation.english_text: Sena! [She runs in screaming.] Cast the killing sword upon me first.

That cannot be! You must feast your eyes on this child falling into the cruel mouth of the goddess of death. Only after that shall I watch in ecstasy as the Chola line bursts into a hundred pieces and scatters into dust.

Stop, Vasanthi, stop! For many years you made my husband yours and turned my life into a moonless sky. I endured it. You sat beside the emperor in the assembly hall like the great empress of the empire. I endured that too. With wicked words you killed me without killing me; even that I endured. Whenever my son rose roaring like a tiger, I stopped at once the sword springing from its sheath and saved your life. Why? You witless woman who holds the golden idol of the Chola land at knife-point—I ask you: why was I patient?
notes: The repeated `I endured` structure, moonless-sky image and unsheathed-sword image are preserved.

translation.english_text: No—love for my husband. You belonged to him. I thought I must not harm what was his and bring grief to my husband. But today you have imprisoned my husband himself. Vasantha Sena, in the name of the patience I have shown until this day, I ask you. It is the country you want, is it not? Take it. Rule your kingdom! The forest is enough for us. Let all of us go.
Ah! Let you go? Do not dream! In another half a moment, the ash-heap of the Chola Empire will be piled at my feet.
Vasantha Sena! If the very form of truth rises as a storm, you will sink into that ash-heap. Beware!
You dare threaten me?

Yes—you. A land where the sky pours rain! A forest where deer roam! A home where honey showers—our Chola realm. You came there bearing the kamandalam of love, devised plot after plot and plundered a beautiful life. I welcomed the woman who came and gave her space to live in pleasure all these days! And today you speak with arrogance: you to rule, we to perish. No! You yourself are performing the aarti for your own destruction. Do not perish in vain!
notes: The land/forest/home parallelism, `love-kamandalam`, rule/perish antithesis and self-aarti image are preserved.

Mother!...... [He cries out.]

Manohara! My unfading lamp of fame! Forgive me, da! Whenever you rose in valour to compose a heroic epic in defence of the greatness of the Chola Empire, it was I—the culprit—who hid the stylus, concealed the palm leaves and stood in your way. My gold, who bore your mother's command upon your head! Even if your own mother now commands you, ‘Destroy injustice,’ you have been brought to a state where you cannot move, my treasure! Ruined. Everything is ruined.
notes: The heroic-epic/stylus/palm-leaf image and repeated maternal address are retained.

translation.english_text: No, Mother......! No! My own mother—now give the order, the command: ‘Destroy injustice!’ The final hour! The final plea! My Tamil Mother! After seeing this outrage—the little jackal that entered this land through a pass opening amid the pleasure-grove, settled here, and today has laid the first token for climbing the throne—will you at least now grant permission? I need no sword, Mother! One spoken word is enough. I need no army, Mother—only let the mother's ban be lifted! Give me no blade, Mother—one glance of the eye is enough—and freedom for you, for me, for everyone. Where is the order, Mother? Give the order. I shall erase these people until no trace of their form remains.
notes: `தமிழ்த் தாயே` remains `Tamil Mother`; the jackal/pass/throne imagery and sword/word, army/ban, blade/glance parallelism are preserved.

translation.english_text: My precious treasure! It was for your father's good that I bound your heroic hands. I bowed my head before this venomous woman. After the very man for whose sake I kept saying patience, patience has himself been locked in prison, where is the greatness left in patience? Manohara! Enough endurance. Rise in a surge!
notes: The `பொறுமை / பெருமை` patience/greatness turn and `பொங்கியெழு` eruptive command are preserved.

source_locator.description: Padmavathi runs to the king's statue.

translation.english_text: [She runs to the king's statue.]
Maharaja! Do you see how our treasured family is being destroyed? Look at Manoharan, bound and writhing. Look at Manoharan, Maharaja! Maharaja!! Maharaja!!!

source_locator.description: Ugrasenan and Vasanthi laugh.

translation.english_text: [Ugrasenan and Vasanthi laugh.]

Why are you laughing? Monkeys leaping in a red-banana grove! Great sinners who came to bend this land, one in the form of a woman, one in the form of a holy man! You who forgot the history the world tells—that those who laughed so have not lived, and those who wept have not been ruined! Little pack of jackals who came by sleight of hand to break the sceptre of the flourishing Tamils! Do not laugh! Pack of villains unable to know the power of tears! Do not laugh, forgetting that tears have accomplished what even the point of a sword has not. Traitors who, amid the afflicted, compose sandhu and sing sindhu—do not laugh, do not laugh...... O soil of the motherland! Look at Manoharan, the sacred lamp of your house! Chola Mother! Look at the agony of the warrior of warriors who placed a victory-garland upon your beautiful shoulder. Look at the son who marked your lovely forehead with tilak from the blood of foreign enemies—alas!—now bound and suffering in the fetters of slavery. O ceremonial hall of the Chola family, how long will you make the form of my victory bow his head amid these useless men? A tender infant—the crown prince! A king who is to rule. O Mother Earth who bears the sinner thirsting to avenge herself upon them all! If it is true that you are grateful; if it is true that the tears of mothers born in the warrior clan possess power; if it is true that the great warrior Manoharan, who has never known how to kneel before an outsider, is my son—let these chains shatter into fragments, let the laughter of the unjust cease, let this very hall collapse into dust. Into dust! Into dust!! Into dust!!!
notes: The speech is preserved in full: red-banana monkeys, woman/holy-man disguises, tears-versus-sword, motherland/Chola Mother, victory-garland, blood-tilak, slavery-fetters and the final threefold dust invocation all remain visible.
`சந்து புனை சிந்து பாடும்` is retained conservatively as `compose sandhu and sing sindhu` rather than replaced by an unsupported literary interpretation.
